# Read_TOC master and clean

```{r}
TOC_master <- read_excel("../TOC/Final_2025_DIC.xlsx", sheet = 1)

TOC_master <- TOC_master %>% filter(Sample_Volume == 15) 
# made a really bad mistake by diluting some samples
# well, DIC generation is governed by pH right? So what happens if we add water to the sample? pH changes.
# Good job Zhang, made a lot of samples unusable LOL
# But hey, we deal with what we have right? 

TOC_master$Conc_final <- TOC_master$Concentration_ppm*((TOC_master$DI_Volume+TOC_master$Sample_Volume)/TOC_master$Sample_Volume)

Samples_only <- TOC_master%>%
                filter(Plot!="Inlet") %>%
                filter(Plot!="Outlet") %>%
                mutate(Treatment = str_extract(Plot, "\\d+")) %>%   # extract digits
                mutate(Treatment = as.factor(Treatment)) 

Inlet_Outlet <- TOC_master%>%
                filter(Plot%in% c("Inlet", "Outlet"))

ggplot(Inlet_Outlet, aes(y=Conc_final, x=Sampling_Date, color = Plot)) + geom_point()

ggplot(Samples_only, aes(y=Conc_final, x=Sampling_Date, color = Treatment)) + geom_point()
```

# DIC over time visualization

```{r}
DIC_graphing <- Samples_only %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Sampling_Date) %>%
  mutate(Conc_final_se = sd(Conc_final)/sqrt(5)) %>%
  summarise(Conc_final = mean(Conc_final),
  Conc_final_se = mean(Conc_final_se))

DIC_over_time <- ggplot(DIC_graphing, aes(x = Sampling_Date, y = Conc_final,  colour =  Treatment))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=Conc_final-Conc_final_se, ymax=Conc_final+Conc_final_se), size=0.5)

DIC_over_time

ggsave(DIC_over_time, filename = "../Figures/DIC_over_time_ERW.jpg", height = 25, width = 25, units = "cm", dpi=400)
```


# Prelimary Stats

```{r}
Samples_only$Sampling_Date_factor <- as.factor(Samples_only$Sampling_Date)

model <- lm(Concentration_ppm~Treatment*Sampling_Date_factor, data = Samples_only)

pls205_diagnostics(model)

anova(model)
means <- emmeans(model, spec = "Treatment", by = "Sampling_Date_factor")
cld(means)

```


# Percolation rate

We assume a percolation rate of 0.21 mm per day.

This are results taken from LaHue an Linquist (2018) https://doi.org/10.1016/j.agwat.2020.106445

![Percolation Rate: Site 1 is the same site as we are using](C:/Users/zhang/Documents/GitHub/ERW/Scripts/Gab_LaHue_Percolation.png)

So a total of 2100 L of water percolates through the field each day per hectare.

0.21 mm = 0.00021 m
1 ha = 10 000 m2
Volume = 0.00021m*10 000 m2 = 2.1m3
2.1m3 = 2100 L 


# Linear interpolation

```{r}

start_date <- as.Date("2025-06-18")
end_date <- as.Date("2025-09-08")
date_seq <- seq.Date(start_date, end_date, by = "day")

DIC_2025_interpolated <- Samples_only %>%
  mutate(Date = Sampling_Date) %>%
  group_by(Plot) %>%
  complete(Date = date_seq) %>%
  ungroup()

DIC_2025_interpolated <- DIC_2025_interpolated %>%
  group_by(Plot) %>%
  mutate(Conc_final = na.approx(Conc_final, rule = 2)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Treatment = str_extract(Plot, "\\d+")) %>%   # extract digits
                mutate(Treatment = as.factor(Treatment)) 

#conc multiplied by water percolation to get a c removal rate
#2100L of water moves through each ha of field per day
#convert mg to kg, each kg gives 1000000mg

DIC_2025_interpolated$Daily_C_removed <- DIC_2025_interpolated$Conc_final*2100/1000000


DIC_2025_rice_seasonal_C_removal <- DIC_2025_interpolated %>%
  group_by(Plot) %>%
  summarize(seasonal_C_removal = sum(Daily_C_removed, na.rm = TRUE))%>% 
            #total_N2O_emissions = sum(N2O_g_ha_day, na.rm = TRUE)) 
  mutate(Period_Year = "Summer_2025") %>%
  mutate(Period = "Summer")%>%
  mutate(Treatment = str_extract(Plot, "\\d+")) %>%   # extract digits
                mutate(Treatment = as.factor(Treatment)) 

ggplot(DIC_2025_interpolated, aes(y=Daily_C_removed, x=Date, color = Plot)) + geom_point()
#ggplot(flux_2025_rice_interpolated, aes(y=N2O_g_ha_day, x=Date, color = Plot)) + geom_point()
```
# Simple stats

```{r}
model <- lm(seasonal_C_removal~Treatment, data=DIC_2025_rice_seasonal_C_removal)

anova(model)

Treatment_means = emmeans(model,spec = 'Treatment')
Treatment_effects = contrast(Treatment_means, method = 'pairwise', adjust = "Tukey")
summary(Treatment_effects)

cld(Treatment_means)

C_removal_seasonal <- DIC_2025_rice_seasonal_C_removal %>%
  group_by(Treatment) %>%
  mutate(seasonal_C_removal_se = sd(seasonal_C_removal)/sqrt(5)) %>%
  summarise(seasonal_C_removal = mean(seasonal_C_removal),
  seasonal_C_removal_se = mean(seasonal_C_removal_se))
```
